measuring and controlling system\nresources utilized by a program.\n\n[Availability](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/intro.html#availability): Unix, not WASI.\n\nSymbolic constants are used to specify particular system resources and to\nrequest usage information about either the current process or its children.\n\nAn [`OSError`](https://docs.python.org/3.14/builtins/exceptions.html#OSError alias of [`OSError`](https://docs.python.org/3.14/builtins/exceptions.html#OSError \"OSError\").\n\n## Resource Limits [¶](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/resource.html\\#resource-limits \"Link to this heading\")\n\nResources usage can be limited using the [`setrlimit()`](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/resource.html#resource.setrlimit \"resource.setrlimit\") function described\nbelow. Each resource is controlled by a pair of limits: a soft limit and a hard\nlimit. The soft limit is the current limit, and may be lowered or raised by a\nprocess over time. The soft limit can never exceed the hard limit. The hard\nlimit can be lowered to any value greater than the soft limit, but not raised.\n(Only processes with the effective UID of the super-user can raise a hard\nlimit.)\n\nThe specific resources that can be limited are system dependent. They are\ndescribed in the _[getrlimit(2)](https://manpages.debian.org/getrlimit(2))_ man page.
